text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Three members of the former management in fishing company Fideco claim that Planning Minister Terje Roed-Larsen probably back dated in 1986 a contract for share-options in the company. This is in disagreement with earlier statments from Roed-Larsen.
- Members of opposition parties are demanding that Prime Minister Torbjoern Jagland intervene in the Roed-Larsen scandal and put an end to the issue.

- Danish brewery Carlsberg may form a copperation agreement with The Coca-Cola Company in Norway. Coca-Cola has terminated the contract with its current partner Orkla ASA. Carlsberg and Coca-Cola are already cooperating in Denmark and also are discussing a cooperation in Sweden.
- State-owned telecommunications group Telenor will reduce prices for services by a total of 1.1 billion crowns. Telenor has been reducing prices for the past eight years.

- A survey commissioned by the government by the Center for Economical Analyses, ECON, shows that immigrants, with the exception of refugees, contribute the same amount to public finances as they receive.
